question.prompt: Mr. \(A\) owns a house worth \(\$10{,}000.\) He sells it to Mr. \(B\) at \(10\%\) profit. Mr. \(B\) sells the house back to Mr. \(A\) at a \(10\%\) loss. Then:

solutions.explanation:
The two percentages use different bases. Mr. A's sale at a \(10\%\) profit gives a price of
\[
10{,}000+0.10(10{,}000)=11{,}000
\]
dollars. Mr. B's \(10\%\) loss is based on the \(\$11{,}000\) he paid, so he sells the house back for
\[
11{,}000-0.10(11{,}000)=9{,}900
\]
dollars.

Mr. A ends with the same house he owned initially. His cash has increased by
\[
11{,}000-9{,}900=1{,}100
\]
dollars, while Mr. B has lost that amount. None of A through D states this result, so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Compare the sale and repurchase payments
